quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #6
										  					
  

40 Questions • Passing Score 32

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: The road ahead curves only to the right.
The road ahead turns sharply to the right.
The road ahead curves right, then left.
The road ahead curves left, then right.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road ahead curves right, then left.
questions.explanation: Warning signs alert drivers to hazards ahead. They are yellow with black markings. This sign warns that the road curves to the right and then to the left.

questions.question: You approach a railroad crossing with a crossbuck sign but no gates or flashing lights. You should:

options.text: Approach with caution and cross only when you are sure no train is coming.
Turn down your radio to listen for a train.
Wait for a flagger to clear you before crossing.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Always approach railroad crossings with caution. Cross only when you know no train is coming from either direction. If a flagger is present, follow their instructions.

questions.question: If another car might hit you, what should you do?

options.text: Sound your horn.
Wave your arms.
Use your emergency lights.
Flash your headlights.

questions.explanation: Use your horn to warn other drivers or pedestrians who may not see you. For example, sound your horn if you think another driver is about to hit you.

questions.question: As a pedestrian, what should you do?

options.text: Always insist on the right-of-way over vehicles in a crosswalk.
Never enter a street or crosswalk when vehicles are approaching.
Enter a crosswalk anytime because drivers must stop.
Use crosswalks only when they are convenient.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never enter a street or crosswalk when vehicles are approaching.
questions.explanation: Do not enter a street or crosswalk when vehicles are approaching. Even though pedestrians have the right-of-way in crosswalks, a nearby vehicle may not be able to stop in time.

questions.question: When turning, drivers should turn into:

options.text: The first available legal lane.
The lane farthest from the direction of travel.
Any lane.
The second-closest available lane.

questions.explanation: Turn into the first available legal lane. This is the safest way to turn because you avoid changing lanes while turning. Crossing fewer lanes reduces the risk of collisions.

questions.question: When a flagger directs traffic in a construction zone, you must:

options.text: Follow the flagger's directions.
Copy other vehicles even if the flagger says otherwise.
Assume the flagger should not be there.
Follow normal traffic laws instead of the flagger.

questions.explanation: Always follow directions from flaggers, signs, and law enforcement in construction zones. Ignoring these instructions is illegal and dangerous to workers.

questions.question: Your power steering stops working while you are driving. You should:

options.text: Honk your horn and turn off the ignition.
Turn on hazard lights and brace yourself.
Steer firmly, slow down, move to a safe area, and stop.
Slam on the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Steer firmly, slow down, move to a safe area, and stop.
questions.explanation: When power steering fails, steering becomes harder. Slow down and carefully move to a safe area off the road, then stop.

questions.question: A common sign of a drunk driver is:

options.text: Weaving between lanes.
Driving slower than normal traffic.
Making sudden, jerky stops.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Signs of drunk driving include weaving, driving too fast or too slow, jerky motions, and sudden stops.

questions.question: Roads freeze quickly when they are:

options.text: Flat.
Curvy.
In the sun.
Shaded.

questions.explanation: In cold or wet weather, be extra careful on shaded roads. Shaded areas freeze before other parts of the road and are the last to thaw.

questions.question: Highway signs that warn about hazardous conditions are called:

options.text: Regulatory signs.
Warning signs.
Information signs.
Guide signs.

questions.explanation: Warning signs alert drivers to potential hazards ahead. Follow warning signs for your safety. Ignoring them can cause accidents.

questions.question: How can you avoid the risks of alcohol-related crashes?

options.text: Decide before drinking that you will not drive.
Say "No thanks, I'm driving" if someone offers you a drink.
Call a taxi.
Do any of the above.

questions.explanation: The best way to avoid drinking and driving is to decide before you drink that you will not drive. Alcohol affects your judgment, so it is harder to make safe decisions after you have been drinking.

questions.question: When stopped by police for a traffic violation or equipment check, you must show:

options.text: Proof of insurance.
Your driver's license.
Proof of vehicle registration.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: You must have your driver's license, proof of registration, and proof of insurance in your vehicle at all times while driving. You must show all three documents if stopped.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: You are entering a one-way street in the wrong direction.
School crossing ahead.
Do not drive in this lane.
Left-turning traffic on green must yield to oncoming traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Left-turning traffic on green must yield to oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: This sign tells drivers that left-turning traffic does not have the right-of-way. Left-turning drivers must wait for oncoming traffic to pass.

questions.question: You must stop for a school bus:

options.text: That is parked on the shoulder with no children in it.
When it approaches you, even if its lights are not flashing.
On a two-lane road when its red lights are flashing.
Whenever the driver waves at you.

questions.correctAnswerText: On a two-lane road when its red lights are flashing.
questions.explanation: You must stop when a school bus has flashing red lights on a two-lane road. Both directions of traffic must stop as long as the red lights are flashing and the stop arm is extended.

questions.question: Driving much slower than the speed limit is:

options.text: Illegal.
Smart.
Safe.
Optional.

questions.explanation: Driving much slower than traffic around you is dangerous and against the law. It blocks other drivers and forces them to change lanes frequently.

questions.question: The most important thing about speed and curves is that you must:

options.text: Drive at the speed limit as you enter the curve, then slow down in the sharpest part.
Slow down before entering the curve.
Speed up gently before entering the curve.
Drive at the speed limit before, during, and after the curve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down before entering the curve.
questions.explanation: Your vehicle's weight and momentum can make it hard to turn. Slow down before entering the curve to keep control of your vehicle.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Watch for drunk drivers.
Curves ahead.
Road is slippery when wet.
Apply brakes quickly.

questions.explanation: This sign warns that the road surface becomes slippery when wet.

questions.question: When you see a flashing red traffic light, you should:

options.text: Drive through if there is no other traffic.
Continue driving since you have the right-of-way.
Stop only if a police officer is nearby.
Treat it like a stop sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Treat it like a stop sign.
questions.explanation: Flashing red lights are used at dangerous intersections. You must treat them the same way as a stop sign.

questions.question: Compared to daytime driving, night driving is:

options.text: Less dangerous.
About the same.
More dangerous.
Easier on your eyes.

questions.explanation: Night driving is more dangerous because it is harder to see, headlights can temporarily blind you, and more tired or impaired drivers are on the road.

questions.question: You should be careful when passing a bicycle because:

options.text: You are moving faster than the bicycle.
The bicycle always has the right-of-way.
Oncoming traffic may not see you pass the bicycle.
The cyclist may swerve into traffic to avoid something on the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: The cyclist may swerve into traffic to avoid something on the road.
questions.explanation: Always be careful when passing a bicycle because the cyclist may suddenly swerve into traffic to avoid an object. Always drive cautiously near bicyclists.

questions.question: As alcohol builds up in your blood, it:

options.text: Slows down your reactions.
Makes you feel more confident.
Makes your body break it down faster.
Reduces the number of driving mistakes.

questions.explanation: As alcohol builds up in your system, it slows your reactions, makes you feel too confident, and causes more driving mistakes.

questions.question: ____ limit your concentration, perception, judgment, and memory.

options.text: Only alcohol above the legal limit can
Alcohol does not
Any amount of alcohol can
Only alcohol above 0.05 percent can

questions.explanation: Any amount of alcohol reduces your concentration, perception, judgment, and memory. Your driving skills will suffer. No one can drink and drive safely.

questions.question: Your blind spot is the area of the road:

options.text: You cannot see without turning your head.
Directly behind your vehicle.
You can see in your rearview mirror.
You can see in your side mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: You cannot see without turning your head.
questions.explanation: Blind spots are areas you cannot see without turning your head. They are located on the sides and behind your vehicle.

questions.question: When you want to make a right turn, your car must be:

options.text: In the center of the street.
Close to the left side of the street.
Close to the right side of the street.
Past the center of the intersection before turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: Close to the right side of the street.
questions.explanation: Before making a right turn, move as far to the right side of the road as possible. Do not cut across other lanes when making any turn.

questions.question: If two vehicles arrive to a four-way stop at the same time:

options.text: The vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.
The vehicle on the right must yield to the vehicle on the left.
Drivers must use hand signals to communicate.
One driver should proceed without stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.
questions.explanation: Vehicles at a four-way stop should go in the order they arrive. If two vehicles arrive at the same time, the vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.

questions.question: Which statement is true?

options.text: Other drivers can follow motorcycles closely.
A motorcycle with two riders is more balanced than one with one rider.
You must completely change lanes when passing a motorcycle.
A motorcycle's brake lights will light up when the rider slows down.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must completely change lanes when passing a motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles are entitled to use a full lane. Move completely into the left lane before passing a motorcycle on the left.

questions.question: It is important to slow down:

options.text: On narrow or winding roads.
At intersections or railroad crossings.
When the road is wet or slippery.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Slow down on narrow or winding roads, near intersections or railroad crossings, on hills, in sharp or blind curves, where there are pedestrians or hazards, and on wet or slippery roads.

questions.question: When approaching a flashing yellow light, drivers should:

options.text: Speed up.
Stop completely.
Turn on their headlights.
Slow down and drive carefully.

questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light warns of a hazard ahead. Slow down and drive carefully.

questions.question: Traffic moving in opposite directions is divided by ____ lines.

options.text: White
Red
Black
Yellow

questions.explanation: Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions.

questions.question: If a vehicle with high beams comes toward you, look toward ____ of the road.

options.text: Either side
The center
The right side
The left side

questions.explanation: If an oncoming vehicle uses high beams and does not dim them, look toward the right side of the road. This keeps you from being blinded and helps you stay on your course until the vehicle passes.

questions.question: When turning left from a multilane, one-way street or highway, which lane should you start from?

options.text: The middle of the intersection.
The right lane.
The left lane.
Any lane.

questions.explanation: Always start a left turn from the left lane on multilane streets and highways.

questions.question: Which statement about railroad crossings is true?

options.text: It is illegal to drive around lowered gates at a crossing.
You must stop at a railroad crossing when a flagger tells you to.
Not all railroad crossings have flashing red signals and gates.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: You must stop when a flagger, stop sign, or warning devices tell you to. Not all crossings have gates or flashing lights. It is illegal to drive around lowered railroad crossing gates.

questions.question: When passing on a multilane highway, what should you do?

options.text: Make sure the passing lane is clear.
Pass only on the right.
Watch for oncoming traffic.
You do not need to signal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure the passing lane is clear.
questions.explanation: Before passing, check that the passing lane is clear and use your turn signal to show you are changing lanes.

questions.question: What should you do when you see a railroad crossing warning sign?

options.text: Drive faster than the train.
Be ready to stop if a train is nearby.
Look for a way around lowered gates.
Assume no trains are coming and drive normally.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready to stop if a train is nearby.
questions.explanation: Railroad warning signs alert drivers that a train may be coming. Always obey these signs and never drive around barriers.

questions.question: If you get stranded in a snowstorm, what should you do?

options.text: Leave the car and go find help.
Lie down in the car and sleep.
Walk into the road to get other drivers' attention.
Stay in your car—you are more likely to be found there.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay in your car—you are more likely to be found there.
questions.explanation: Stay in your car and wait for help. Rescue teams will find you more easily if you remain in your vehicle. Walking in a snowstorm is dangerous.

questions.question: What is true about drowsy drivers?

options.text: They should drink strong black coffee to stay awake.
They can drive so poorly that they look drunk.
They can stay alert by opening a window and turning up the radio.
They are usually older drivers only.

questions.correctAnswerText: They can drive so poorly that they look drunk.
questions.explanation: Drowsy drivers can drive poorly and appear drunk. Opening a window, playing the radio, or drinking coffee is not enough to keep a drowsy driver alert.

questions.question: When an emergency vehicle with sirens and flashing lights approaches you, what must you do?

options.text: Pull to the right and stop.
Pull to the right and slow down.
Pull to the right and turn on your four-way flashers.
Stop and let it pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the right and stop.
questions.explanation: When an emergency vehicle approaches with lights, sirens, or other warnings, you must immediately drive to the right side of the road and stop.

questions.question: Who must wear a seat belt by law in a moving vehicle?

options.text: Anyone under 18 years old.
Adult passengers.
The driver.
Backseat passengers.

questions.explanation: By law, anyone under 18 must wear a seat belt in a moving vehicle. Everyone should wear a seat belt to prevent injury or death in a crash.

questions.question: What should you do with loose objects in your car?

options.text: Put them on the back seat.
Put them on the dashboard.
Secure them to avoid hazards.
Keep them on a back shelf.

questions.explanation: Loose objects can fly through your car during a crash and cause serious injury. Do not put heavy or sharp objects on the dashboard or rear shelf.

questions.question: When a school bus stops with its stop arm extended, what should you do?

options.text: Come to a complete stop and wait.
Honk your horn before passing on the left.
Keep driving when you think children are done exiting.
Pass the bus before the door opens.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a complete stop and wait.
questions.explanation: When a school bus is stopped with its stop arm extended, you must come to a complete stop. Do not proceed until the stop arm is raised.
